research_question: Why does tectonic activity continue to raise the Himalayas?

sources.title: The Himalayas
notes: India collided with Eurasia roughly 40–50 million years ago; convergence continues to deform and thicken the crust.

sources.title: This Dynamic Earth: The Story of Plate Tectonics
notes: Plate motion, faulting and crustal deformation drive mountain building; uplift and erosion operate at the same time.

sources.title: Himalayan tectonics and earthquakes
sources.publisher: U.S. Geological Survey Earthquake Hazards Program
notes: The plate boundary remains active and produces earthquakes; local vertical motion varies and should not be described as uniform uplift everywhere.
